Korean multi-step skin-care regimen that went global from 2011, beginning with the double cleanse.
tech: Double cleanse: oil-based cleanser to melt make-up and sunscreen, then a water-based cleanser; then toner, essence, serum, sheet mask, moisturiser, sunscreen.
mat: cleansing oils and balms, low-pH gel and foam cleansers, essences, sheet masks
auth: Korean labelling and authorised sellers; counterfeit risk to verify per brand.

d: Japanese hydration-first skin care, with the cleansing oil (Shu Uemura, 1960) and keshōsui lotion pressed into the skin after cleansing.
tech: Oil cleanse, then keshōsui pressed in by hand in layers rather than wiped on, then milk or cream.
mat: cleansing oils, hyaluronic and rice- or sake-based lotions
auth: Japanese-market packaging with Japanese ingredient labels; to verify per product.

p: Formalised in the Ming dynasty (1368–1644); facial use popular worldwide from 2016–2022

mat: Jade and other stones, ceramic spoons, coins, water buffalo horn
ctr: Palace Museum, Beijing (Qing jade roller set)
auth: Antique pieces are museum-held; modern tools are mass-made, so judge by stone and finish rather than claims of tradition.

p: Known in the West from 2011 (BB cream) onward

mat: Green tea, orchid, soybean, snail mucin, bee venom
auth: Check brand origin and country of manufacture on the label.

mat: Yuzu, camellia oil, rice, green tea, konjac
auth: Check brand origin and country of manufacture on the label.
